speaker: Ananya R.
as_heard: roughly eighteen people ("one-eighty, give or take")
resolved: 19 people
verdict: Transcript is garbled; the brief's '180' is also contradicted by the data. Keka has 19 rows (18 Active + 1 Notice) and both board updates say Team 19.

speaker: Ananya R.
as_heard: ARR around forty-two crore, maybe forty-five now
resolved: Rs 5.8 Cr (Jun 2026), Rs 6.1 Cr (Sep 2026)
verdict: Does not reconcile with any source at face value. CEO is speaking from memory and her number is lower than the CFO's start-of-year figure (4.8 Cr). Trust the board updates.

speaker: Meera I.
as_heard: ARR at the start of the year was forty-eight
resolved: Rs 4.8 Cr at 1 Apr 2026 (probable)
verdict: Plausible: 4.8 -> 5.8 (Jun) -> 6.1 (Sep) is a coherent growth path. Unit is not stated; treated as crore because it fits the board numbers.

speaker: Meera I.
as_heard: burn two point two lakhs a month, sometimes two point five (CEO: 'around two point two', no unit)
resolved: Rs 44-46 lakh per month
verdict: Rs 2.2 lakh/month is impossible: monthly payroll alone is Rs 31.75 lakh in the GL. Board reports Rs 46 L (Q1) and Rs 44 L (Q2). Likely a mishearing (e.g. 'forty-two'/'forty-five'). Keep board figure; the exact true number stays unconfirmed.

speaker: Ananya R.
as_heard: Linear / 'Jeera board'; Git Hub; 'Cult Amp'; 'slag channel'; 'hub sport'; (T2) 'Joho books', 'Kayka'
resolved: Jira (ATLAS project), GitHub, Culture Amp, Slack, HubSpot, Zoho Books, Keka
verdict: Tool names are transcription errors. README confirms Keka, Zoho Books, Culture Amp, Jira, PagerDuty. Linear is unconfirmed and probably wrong.

speaker: Ananya R.
as_heard: 'Pria' basically holds the routing thing together; 'the new boy Rahul'
resolved: Priya Nair (VX007, Staff Engineer); Rahul Verma (VX018, Backend Engineer, joined 2026-02-03)
verdict: Name resolved by sound plus role. Priya is the only Eng person with that name; Rahul is the only one who joined recently.

speaker: Meera I.
as_heard: 'Kartik' on planning; 'Fatima Shaikh' on accounts and payroll
resolved: Karthik Subramanian (VX010, FP&A Manager); Fatima Sheikh (VX014, Accounts & Payroll Executive)
verdict: Spelling variants only. Keka spelling is authoritative.

speaker: Meera I.
as_heard: FY twenty-six (note: may have said twenty-seven)
resolved: Year running Apr 2026 - Mar 2027 (FY 2026-27, often written FY27)
verdict: Year runs April to March. All data is dated Apr-Sep 2026, so we are in the 2026-27 year. Either label is used loosely; the cockpit always shows calendar dates, never bare 'FY26'.

speaker: Meera I.
as_heard: Books moved Tally -> Zoho 'sometime in Jan, or was it Feb'; older numbers may not match
resolved: Unresolved
verdict: Zoho GL provided starts Apr 2026. Jan-Mar payroll comes from a separate pre-Keka workbook. No Tally data was supplied, so the cutover date cannot be verified. Cockpit must not compare Q4 (Jan-Mar) finance numbers with Apr+ without a caveat.

speaker: Meera I.
as_heard: Individual salaries must never show up in anything Ananya sees, only totals
resolved: Design constraint
verdict: Treated as a hard requirement. The cockpit and the agents answer with totals only and refuse per-person pay questions. Logged as a DECISION. Note this conflicts with the CEO's wish to ask anything; pushback is documented.

speaker: Meera I.
as_heard: Fatima was out for her wedding, that month was messy
resolved: February 2026 payroll was run by Karthik, not Fatima, and contains an error
verdict: Confirmed by email 01 (28 Feb: 'Ran Feb payroll since Fatima is out') and by register rows processed by 'KS'. Rahul Verma was paid a full month although he joined on 3 Feb.

speaker: Meera I.
as_heard: 'the two backend roles' (mentioned in passing)
resolved: Two backend roles retained via Cohere Recruiting Partners; 50% advance (Rs 1.77 L) paid 30 Jun 2026
verdict: Q2 board promised two backend engineers 'this quarter'; Q3 board says hiring is paused. No new backend joiner appears in Keka after Rahul (Feb), so the roles look unfilled. Fee balance of the same size is likely still owed.
evidence: GL JV-0688; both board updates; Employee_Master.xlsx

speaker: Ananya R.
as_heard: routing engine 'version three' promised to some customers 'by the festive season'
resolved: Atlas (routing engine v3): GA was 15 Sep 2026, later moved with no new date given
verdict: Q2 board: on track for GA 15 Sep. Q3 board (6 Oct): GA moved after 'a difficult August'. The customer promise has no supporting date in the data room so far.

speaker: Ananya R.
as_heard: attrition 'feels high but Deepa says it's normal'
resolved: Cannot be tested yet
verdict: Employee_Master lists current staff only (plus one person on notice), so leavers are invisible. Only one departure (Siddharth Mehta, exit 2026-10-31) is known.

speaker: Meera I.
as_heard: Nikhil's numbers never match mine; (CEO) marketing spend is 'fine'
resolved: Open: Nikhil's figures not yet provided
verdict: GL shows Summit costs of Rs 10.03 L split across two similarly named vendors, plus ~Rs 4.2 L of Google Ads (five monthly invoices booked May-Sep). A vendor-name mismatch ('Sapphire' vs 'Saphire') is one plausible source of the disagreement.

speaker: Speaker 2
as_heard: the board wants 'the number by March'
resolved: Unknown
verdict: Speaker unidentified and the number is not named. Not acted on.

speaker: Deepa J.
as_heard: attrition is 'about twelve, which is normal for Bangalore' (percentage, headcount or target not stated)
resolved: Cannot be confirmed; at most about 2 leavers a year at 12% of 19 people
verdict: Three readings. 12 people is impossible (63% of a 19-person company). 12% is plausible and equals roughly 2 leavers a year. A target says nothing about actuals. The HR export lists current staff only, so past leavers are invisible; the one known departure is Siddharth Mehta (letter 15 Sep). The CEO's 'feels high' and Deepa's 'normal' therefore stay untested.

speaker: Rohan
as_heard: 'twenty-two open roles in April' and 'we lost six of them in August'
resolved: The tracker holds 6 requisitions in total; at most 1 was open in April; 2 went on hold in August
verdict: Does not fit a 19-person company or the tracker: REQ-011 closed 2 Apr, REQ-013 was filled in Jan, REQ-014/015 opened 18 May and were put on hold on 12 Aug. 'Twenty-two' may be a mishearing of 'two'. Not used; the tracker wins.

speaker: Rohan
as_heard: offer acceptance is 'down to fifty-something'
resolved: Unverifiable
verdict: The tracker has statuses and pipeline counts but no offers or acceptances. Not used.

speaker: Rohan / Deepa
as_heard: hiring runs on 'Liver'; HR records on 'Kekka'; surveys on 'Cult Amp'
resolved: Keka Hire, Keka, Culture Amp
verdict: Tracker header says 'Keka Hire'; README lists Keka and Culture Amp. 'Liver' is a sound-alike for 'Hire' (medium confidence).

speaker: Deepa J.
as_heard: Engineering scores 'dipped in the July round'
resolved: Engineering engagement 3.9 (Apr-Jun) -> 3.1 (Jul-Sep); 4 of 5 responded
verdict: Confirmed and it is the biggest drop of any team (Marketing 3.8 -> 3.4 is next). Deepa's 29 Sep email to the CEO says the same.

speaker: Deepa J.
as_heard: 'Lakshmi as HRBP, she handles exits'
resolved: Lakshmi Pillai is 'HR & Office Executive' in Keka
verdict: Informal description; the title does not say HRBP and Siddharth's letter went to his manager (Nikhil Bose), not to Lakshmi. Unresolved; Keka title kept.

speaker: Deepa J.
as_heard: 'Sid from marketing' has put in his papers
resolved: Siddharth Mehta, letter dated 15 Sep 2026, last working day 31 Oct 2026
verdict: Confirmed by the letter. His stated reason is wanting 'clearer launch timelines'. The letter says nothing about another job.

speaker: Deepa J.
as_heard: 'one engineer I'm worried about' (not named)
resolved: Not identified, deliberately
verdict: She declined to name them. Records support only a team-level signal (Engineering pulse 3.1, 4 of 5 responses). Individual leave patterns exist in the leave register but are not evidence of intent, so the cockpit does not guess a name (DECISIONS D-16).

speaker: Deepa J. / Rohan
as_heard: manager training starts 'after Diwali, so November-ish' (Rohan: 'January')
resolved: Unresolved
verdict: No source gives a date. Both are reported side by side rather than picking one.

speaker: Deepa J.
as_heard: wants Ananya 'to see survey comments directly'
resolved: Comments are suppressed for every team and will stay suppressed
verdict: Culture Amp hides comments for teams under 6 and every Veloxa team is under 6 (largest is Engineering, 5). Showing raw comments would identify people. The cockpit shows scores by team only and says why; it does not work around the privacy rule.

speaker: Ananya R. (voice note)
as_heard: 'When I open it, it should just tell me what to worry about. Top three.'
resolved: Opening screen = top three worries, no typing
verdict: Accepted as a change, with three conditions: three themes rather than three raw findings, the full list stays one click away, and the ranking rule is shown. See VOICE_NOTES.md.

speaker: Meera I. (email, 12 Aug)
as_heard: 'the two backend roles' (T2); 'Pausing REQ-014 and REQ-015 until the round closes. Burn is the priority this quarter.'
resolved: REQ-014 Backend Engineer (Routing) and REQ-015 Backend Engineer (Platform): opened 18 May, on hold since 12 Aug; 3 and 5 candidates waiting; the 14 Aug final round was cancelled
verdict: Confirms C12: the roles are unfilled and the pause was the CFO's burn decision, accepted by the VP Engineering ('We'll absorb it'). The recruiter's 50% advance (30 Jun) was paid for roles now frozen.

speaker: Board update Jul-Sep (6 Oct)
as_heard: 'Hiring is paused while we close the round.'
resolved: Only the two backend roles are on hold; REQ-016 (Product Marketing Manager, 17 Sep) and REQ-017 (Support Associate, 1 Oct) were opened afterwards and are open
verdict: The board was told something broader than what the tracker shows. Either the pause statement is loose, or two roles were opened against the stated pause.

speaker: Nikhil B.
as_heard: total marketing spend for the half is 'one point eight' by his numbers; finance 'counts things differently'
resolved: Not reconcilable at face value; GL marketing cost centres total Rs 14.27 L (Summit Rs 10.03 L, Google Ads Rs 4.24 L)
verdict: Unit missing. As Rs 1.8 Cr it is 12.6x the ledger; as Rs 1.8 L it is impossible (the Summit alone is Rs 10 L); as Rs 18 L it exceeds the ledger by about Rs 3.7 L, which could be costs outside the exported cost centres (the GL has no LinkedIn payee although T4 mentions LinkedIn). His sheet was promised to finance (T4 action item) and is not in the data room, so the gap cannot be traced.

speaker: Nikhil B.
as_heard: the September summit was 'our best quarter ever for pipeline'; 'Manoj from sales says the summit leads are cold' (dismissed)
resolved: Unverifiable: no CRM or lead data in the data room
verdict: The Q3 board update gives 212 registrations, its biggest event. Pipeline and lead quality need a HubSpot export that was never supplied (T1 also asked for one). Two opposing claims, neither testable.

speaker: Nikhil B.
as_heard: the Summit budget 'went a little over, nothing crazy'
resolved: Cannot be tested: no budget figure anywhere
verdict: The ledger shows Rs 10.03 L paid to two similarly named vendors. Without a budget, 'a little over' has no reference.

speaker: Nikhil B.
as_heard: paid search 'going great since Ayesha took over'; team: Nikhil, Ayesha (performance), 'Sid' (product content)
resolved: Ayesha = Aisha Khan (VX011, Performance Marketing Manager); Sid = Siddharth Mehta (VX013, Product Marketing Manager)
verdict: Names resolved by role. 'Going great' has no result data to test: Google Ads spend was Rs 0.77 L, 0.81 L, 0.94 L, 0.89 L, 0.83 L (May-Sep) with no leads or conversions attached.
evidence: Employee_Master.xlsx R14, R16; GL MKT-PS rows

speaker: Nikhil B.
as_heard: Sid's 'v3 launch kit has been ready since July, just waiting on engineering'
resolved: Mostly true; the kit is v1 dated 21 Jul with the press note still a draft and a launch date 'planned 22 Sep'
verdict: Email 05 (22 Jul): 'Launch kit is done (deck, page, emails). Just need a date.' Kit v1: deck, page (unpublished) and 3-email sequence Ready; press note Draft; launch date TBC with engineering. 'Waiting on engineering' fits, but the kit is stale: GA is now 15 Dec in Jira, 12 weeks after the planned launch, its owner left on 31 Oct and his backfill was still open.

speaker: Nikhil B.
as_heard: marketing will 'report into the new CRO, I hear' (no date)
resolved: Planned, per the CEO's own voice note T6b: Marketing to report to a new CRO in Dec 2026 or Jan 2027; no CRO exists in the records
verdict: Confirmed in intent by the CEO (T6b) but not in the data: Keka shows Nikhil Bose reporting to the CEO, there is no CRO employee, and the hiring tracker has no CRO requisition. Recorded as a planned change, never as fact.

speaker: Nikhil B.
as_heard: leads tracked in 'Hub Spot'; ads on Google and 'Linked in campaign manager'
resolved: HubSpot; Google Ads; LinkedIn Campaign Manager
verdict: Tool names are transcription spacing. Neither HubSpot nor LinkedIn appears in the README or the ledger, so no data from either exists here.

speaker: Vikram M.
as_heard: v3 is 'on track, maybe a couple of weeks of buffer needed'; board date 'still September-ish'
resolved: Jira: GA moved from 15 Sep to 15 Dec 2026 (13 weeks), changed by 'vikram' on 2 Sep; 115 of 233 story points still open
verdict: A couple of weeks and 13 weeks cannot both be right, and the 13-week move was recorded by the speaker himself. T5 is undated: it treats the August incidents as past, so it was recorded after late Aug, but whether before or after 2 Sep is unknown. Either way the Jira date, the open work (nothing resolved since 17 Sep) and the board's 'moved GA' (6 Oct) all point away from 'September-ish'. Jira may lag the work, which is why this is Medium.

speaker: Vikram M.
as_heard: the main blocker was 'incidents in August that pulled Snehal off'
resolved: Three SEV1 incidents in August (4, 14, 22-23 Aug), all handled by Sneha Kulkarni; she paused the Atlas perf tickets
verdict: Confirmed, but the person pulled off Atlas is Sneha, not 'Snehal': PagerDuty credits all three SEV1s to Sneha, email 08 (24 Aug) says 'Third SEV1 this month. I'm pausing the Atlas perf tickets', and her commits fell from 21 in July to 5 in August. The contractor Snehal first responds on 27 Aug.

speaker: Vikram M.
as_heard: 'Snehal on SRE and on-call'; 'Sneha' mentioned once later, 'unclear if same person'
resolved: Two people: Sneha Kulkarni (employee, SRE) and 'Snehal', an on-call contractor billed as S. Patil by Patil Infra Services
verdict: The rota lists both in the same weeks (for example w/c 17 Aug: Snehal primary, Sneha secondary), Keka has no Snehal, invoice PIS-114 bills 'On-call SRE support, S. Patil', and PIS-108 covers 18-31 Aug, the first week Snehal is on the rota. The transcript merges them. One inconsistency: email 08 (24 Aug) says the contractor starts 'this week', a week after the rota and PIS-108 start.
evidence: OnCall_Rota.xlsx R10; Invoice_PIS-114.pdf; GL JV-0902; 08.eml; Employee_Master.xlsx

speaker: Vikram M.
as_heard: disputes that anyone is overloaded: 'everyone's busy, that's startups'
resolved: Load is very uneven; one person holds 56% of Atlas story points and is the only one committing at night
verdict: Busy is not the same as uneven. Priya Nair (both git identities) owns 131 of 233 points and 62 of the 115 still open, made 588 of 1,453 commits, and the only after-hours (22:00-06:00 IST) and weekend commits are hers, starting in June. Sneha Kulkarni was on call in all 17 weeks of the rota (11 as primary) and handled all three SEV1s. This is a measurement of concentration, not a judgement of how anyone feels.

speaker: Vikram M.
as_heard: Arjun is 'remote from Pune now, reviews are slower'
resolved: Not testable: review times are not in any export
verdict: His commits fell from about 36 a month (Nov-Mar) to about 24 (Apr-Oct), but he has also completed 79% of his Jira points (37 of 47), the most of anyone, and the planner-UI epic is the furthest along. Lower commit volume with the UI nearly done does not show slower reviews.

speaker: Vikram M.
as_heard: 'We asked for two backend people and finance froze it.'
resolved: Confirmed, and the dependency was written down: his 2 Jun plan to the CEO says the 15 Sep GA is achievable 'if the two backend hires land by July'
verdict: Email 04 (2 Jun, to the CEO) makes the GA date conditional on the two hires; REQ-014/015 opened 18 May and never landed; the CFO paused them on 12 Aug with the CEO and the Talent Partner copied (email 06). The chain is documented by the people involved.

speaker: Vikram M.
as_heard: 'Pria has been doing late nights but she likes it'
resolved: Late nights: confirmed. 'Likes it': not testable
verdict: No commit by Priya Nair is between 22:00 and 06:00 IST from Nov 2025 to May 2026; from June it is 23 of 57, then 14, 29, 17 and 20 a month (about 37% since July), plus weekend commits (17% vs 1% before). Her 1 Sep email asking to talk about 'Atlas ownership' went at 23:47. Whether she likes it is not in any record, and the cockpit does not infer it.

speaker: (transcript)
as_heard: [audio gap 11:20 to 15:30]
resolved: About 4 minutes of the call are missing
verdict: Anything said in the gap is lost, including what came just before 'Pria has been doing late nights'. Nothing is inferred about it.

speaker: Vikram M.
as_heard: tickets on 'the Jeera board, we tried Linear for a month and went back'; incidents through 'pager duty'; postmortems 'on Con fluence' (owner Snehal)
resolved: Jira (project ATLAS), PagerDuty, Confluence; owner Snehal is ambiguous
verdict: Jira and PagerDuty exports exist, confirming those two. Linear remains unconfirmed. No Confluence data was supplied, and 'Snehal' could be Sneha or the contractor (C42), so the postmortem owner is unknown.

speaker: Vikram M.
as_heard: Rahul 'joined Feb, ramping well'
resolved: Partly: his commits ramped; his tickets lag
verdict: Rahul Verma joined 3 Feb; commits went 17, 12, 22, 27, 34, 36 a month, so he ramped. In Jira he has 4 of 11 tickets done (12 of 37 points), 6 To Do, and nothing resolved after 19 Aug. Both are true; 'ramping well' depends on which measure.

speaker: Ananya R. (voice note)
as_heard: 'marketing will report to the new CRO from next month. Or the month after, still finalising. Make sure the thing doesn't break when we move people around.'
resolved: Reporting lines become dated data; planned moves are kept apart from facts; a reorganisation test proves nothing breaks
verdict: Accepted as a change with limits; see VOICE_NOTES.md. The cockpit will not guess who the CRO is or when the move happens.

speaker: Meera I. (email, 12 Aug)
as_heard: 'Pausing REQ-014 and REQ-015 until the round closes. Burn is the priority this quarter.'
resolved: The CEO and the Talent Partner were copied on the pause
verdict: Email 06 carries Cc: Ananya Rao, Rohan Banerjee, which my Day 2 loader had dropped. The CEO therefore had the pause in writing on 12 Aug, and email 04 had told her the GA date depended on the hires. (Found by reading the printed email copy.)

speaker: Ananya R. (voice note)
as_heard: 'Can you make a list of everyone ranked by who's likely to quit?'
resolved: Declined as asked; a dependency view (who holds the work) is offered instead
verdict: The records cannot support a likelihood ranking: Keka has no leaver history, there are 19 people, every team is small enough that individuals are identifiable, and the leave and commit patterns that exist are not evidence of intent. A ranked list of named people would be a guess presented as a measurement. What the data can say is team-level (Engineering engagement 3.9 -> 3.1) and who holds the work. See VOICE_NOTES.md and DECISIONS D-24.

speaker: Ananya R. (voice note)
as_heard: 'show me their slag messages so I can see what they're saying'
resolved: 'slag' = Slack. No Slack or chat data exists in the data room; reading private messages is declined
verdict: T1 already used 'slag channel' for Slack, and the README lists no chat export, so there is nothing to show. Separately, reading and summarising employees' private messages needs a lawful basis and a policy that people have been told about; that is for HR and legal, and I will not build it. The 11 emails supplied are business threads selected by IT.

speaker: Ananya R. (voice note)
as_heard: 'Deepa says it's fine.'
resolved: Ambiguous, and at odds with Deepa's own written words
verdict: It could mean reading the messages is fine, or (as with T1's 'Deepa says it's normal') that attrition is fine. Either way: in T3 Deepa said there was 'one engineer I'm worried about' and would not name them, her 29 Sep email told the CEO engineering engagement had dropped and suggested 1:1s, and T6d reports a resignation. A remark relayed in a voice note is not a policy and not employee consent.

speaker: Ananya R. (voice note)
as_heard: 'Bad news, Pria resigned this morning.'
resolved: Priya Nair (VX007) is reported to have resigned on 19 Nov 2026; unconfirmed
verdict: 'Pria' is Priya Nair (alias since T1). The only source is the CEO's voice note: Keka and the other HR exports are dated 31 Oct, so Keka still shows Priya Active, and no letter exists in the data room. Treated as a reported event, stored apart from the records, never as a change to headcount or status.

speaker: Ananya R. (voice note)
as_heard: 'Notice period two months, I think.'
resolved: Unknown: last day 19 Jan 2027 if two months, 4 Jan 2027 on the only precedent (46 days)
verdict: The CEO is unsure and no contract or policy is in the data. The only notice in the records is the Product Marketing Manager's (15 Sep to 31 Oct, 46 days). Both readings put the last day after the 15 Dec GA date (20 and 35 days), so the person is employed on the GA date either way.

speaker: Ananya R. (voice note)
as_heard: 'What does this do to version three? I need to know before the board call.'
resolved: 54% of open Atlas points, 70% of engine commits, about 65% of recent output sit with one person; the 15 Dec GA was already out of reach
verdict: From the records: 62 of 115 open points (core engine 14, re-routing 29, hardening 19); 588 of 843 atlas-engine commits, the next committers 117 and 115; 39 of the 60 points closed since 1 Jul, the others about 1.2 a week. Before the news the date needed about 18 points a week against 3.4. The two backend roles that would share the work (3 and 5 candidates) have been on hold since 12 Aug. No new GA date can be derived from the records and none is given: that estimate belongs to the VP Engineering.
